case_assessment.summary: The graph captures the main physical accident sequence: operators reopened the sampling system, the insufficiently tightened connector failed, and sulfuric acid sprayed continuously, causing harmful chemical exposure. The main improvements are to restore the omitted location context from the extracted scenario, correct one weak pressure-to-dispersion edge, and replace the hazard node's stitched evidence with a single verbatim quote.
main_problems: The extracted location node for the acid sampling station in the alkylation unit is missing from the final graph.
The edge from low pressure directly to dispersion is weak; the cited pressure condition more directly supports the continuing release after failure.
The hazard consequence node uses a stitched, non-verbatim evidence string instead of a direct quote from the source text.

node_updates.current_state: Evidence is a stitched summary with ellipses rather than a single verbatim quote from the source.
node_updates.suggested_state: Use a single direct quote such as: "concentrated sulfuric acid sprayed two workers following a mechanical integrity failure of a ¾-inch tubing connector adjacent to the acid sampling station."
node_updates.reason: The schema requires direct quoted evidence, and the current H1 evidence is assembled from multiple phrases.
node_updates.evidence: concentrated sulfuric acid sprayed two workers following a mechanical integrity failure of a ¾-inch tubing connector adjacent to the acid sampling station.

node_updates.current_state: The node name "Toxicity dispersion" is used without clarifying that the actual harm mechanism was corrosive sulfuric acid spray causing burns.
node_updates.suggested_state: Clarify in the explanation that "Toxicity dispersion" is the closest allowed schema category for a corrosive sulfuric acid release/spray that caused worker chemical burns.
node_updates.reason: This improves semantic precision while keeping the allowed schema label unchanged.
node_updates.evidence: suffered first and second degree chemical burns

node_additions.suggested_name: Acid sampling station in the alkylation unit
node_additions.reason: This location was part of the extracted scenario and is explicitly identified in the report, but it was omitted from the final graph.
node_additions.evidence: adjacent to the acid sampling station

edge_additions.reason: The cited pressure condition more directly supports the sustained discharge/continuous release after the connector failed than it supports dispersion itself.
edge_additions.evidence: acid continued to spray out of the failed tubing for over two hours from a nearly 100,000-gallon acid settler that was operating below 100 pounds per square inch gauge (psig)

edge_deletions.reason: The source text supports pressure as part of the driving force for the ongoing release, but does not directly support low pressure as the cause of dispersion.
edge_deletions.evidence: acid continued to spray out of the failed tubing for over two hours from a nearly 100,000-gallon acid settler that was operating below 100 pounds per square inch gauge (psig)

issues_summary.description: The final graph dropped the extracted location context for the acid sampling station in the alkylation unit.
C2 -> C11 is physically weak; the pressure condition is better linked to the continuing release than to dispersion.
H1 evidence is not a single verbatim quote from the source text.
The hazard label "Toxicity dispersion" should be explicitly explained as a best-fit schema category for corrosive sulfuric acid spray/burn exposure.
